acme_sre: Hey team — since we moved our worker image to Debian bookworm and switched to an editable install in CI, our runtime fails with ImportError for the SDK async client. We do `pip install -e .[async]` as part of the Docker build. Error on start: `ImportError: No module named 'redwood.async_client'`. Repro steps: build image with Dockerfile, start container, run app.
support_zoe: Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste the exact pip/pip3 and python versions from inside the container and your pyproject/pyproject extras snippet? Also upload the full import traceback if you have it.
acme_sre: Sure — here's the quick output from the container:
```
# python --version
Python 3.10.12
# pip --version
pip 20.3.4 from /usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/pip (python 3.10)
# pip freeze | grep redwood
redwood-sdk @ file:///src/ (dev)
```
Traceback:
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/app/main.py", line 2, in <module>
    from redwood.async_client import AsyncRedwood
ImportError: No module named 'redwood.async_client'
```
pyproject snippet:
```
[project]
name = "my-worker"

[project.optional-dependencies]
async = ["redwood-sdk[async]"]
```
devex_eli: Thanks — two likely things here:
1) pip 20's editable behaviour + PEP 517/518 build-backend interactions often mean extras referenced in an editable install don't get materialized into site-packages the way a normal install does. In short: editable + extras is flaky on older pip/setuptools.
2) The SDK layout changed to use namespace packages for some submodules; when installed as an editable project without the built wheel/install step the package metadata that exposes submodules can be different.
Quick checks:
- run `python -c \"import pkgutil; print(list(pkgutil.iter_modules())[:50])\" to confirm whether redwood package shows submodules
- check `pip show redwood-sdk` and look at `Location` vs where your app imports from

support_zoe: Concrete reproducible workarounds we've used internally:
- easiest: avoid editable installs in CI for production builds. Build a wheel and install it: 
```
python -m pip install --upgrade pip build wheel setuptools
python -m build -w -o /dist
python -m pip install /dist/redwood_sdk-*.whl
```
This ensures extras are included and the wheel pins modules as expected.
- if you need editable installs during local development, make sure pip/setuptools are recent (pip >= 23.0, setuptools >= 65) and use the new editable support (PEP 660). Example:
```
python -m pip install --upgrade pip setuptools build
python -m pip install -e .[async]
```
But note: some environments (older distro packages) still have incompatible pip bootstraps.
sara_engineer: If you're using poetry in dev, you can test with:
```
poetry add ../path/to/redwood-sdk -E async
# or in pyproject
[tool.poetry.dependencies]
redwood-sdk = {path = "../path/to/redwood-sdk", extras = ["async"]}
```
Poetry will handle the extras correctly even in path deps.
acme_sre: OK trying the wheel path now in CI. Quick question — why did it work locally for devs who just do `pip install -e .`? They didn't see the import error.
devex_eli: Locals often have a different environment: newer pip from user installs, or developers had previously installed the package globally/wheel so the editable overlay didn't matter. Also check PYTHONPATH/venv: if your Docker image enables site-packages from system or has old installs it can change resolution.
support_zoe: Helpful debugging snippet to run in the failing container:
```
python - <<'PY'
import sys, importlib, pkgutil
print('sys.path:', sys.path[:6])
print('pip list sample:')
import subprocess
print(subprocess.check_output([sys.executable, '-m', 'pip', 'freeze']).decode().splitlines()[:20])
print('module search for redwood:')
print([m for m in pkgutil.iter_modules() if 'redwood' in m.name])
PY
```
acme_sre: Build changed to wheel-based install and bumped pip in Dockerfile. After re-running CI the service starts and import is OK. Quick log:
```
# pip --version
pip 23.2.1
# pip install /dist/redwood_sdk-0.12.1-py3-none-any.whl
# python -c \"from redwood.async_client import AsyncRedwood; print('ok')\" 
ok
```
support_zoe: Great — sounds like the wheel + pip upgrade fixed the packaging edge-case. We'll add a short KB entry for editable+extras issues and recommended CI pattern.
